grading_system.evidence: You must meet the following minimum credit requirements in order to graduate from Otter Valley Union High School. ... TOTAL 26.5
grading_system.min_score_to_earn_credit: 65 (numeric course grade; 65 is the minimum grade to earn the course credit)

schedule.evidence: Your schedule may include both full-credit (1.0) and half-credit (0.5) courses. Grades are calculated as the weighted average of two semesters and the final exam.

credit_definition.text: 1.0 credit = a full-credit (year) course; 0.5 credit = a half-credit (semester) course.
credit_definition.evidence: Your schedule may include both full-credit (1.0) and half-credit (0.5) courses.

course_load.min_courses_or_credits: Senior partial day requires a minimum of 3.0 credits of academic courses each semester; full-time course load not stated
course_load.evidence: Students requesting a senior partial day must register for a minimum of three (3.0) credits of academic courses during each semester.

local_grad_requirements.conversion_note: Catalog credits are standard credits (1.0 = full-credit course, 0.5 = half-credit course); no conversion needed. Distribution: English 5.0, social studies 4.0, math 3.0, science 3.0, PE 1.5, FACS/Health 0.5, fine arts 2.0, personal finance 0.5, electives 7.0. Grade-level minimums: 7.0 (10th), 14.0 (11th), 21.0 (12th).

notes: Credit-based graduation with numeric grading (A-F scale; 65 minimum to earn credit, p.10). No proficiency-based graduation requirement is stated; mission-level 'Essential Vital Results' and course-level 'Content Proficiencies' (p.6, course descriptions) are not graduation rules. Personal Finance 0.5 and FACS/Health 0.5 are required. Weighted courses carry +.05 or +.08 credit weighting for GPA only (p.9). Schedule structure (periods or blocks per day, number of courses at once) is not stated; the only course-count statement is the 3.0-credit senior partial-day minimum per semester. Senior partial-day, PLP needed for dual enrollment voucher (p.7). Pass/Fail option exists for some seniors (p.12). Source is the catalog PDF text (2026-27 program of studies).
